# frankbueltge.de

> The personal site of Frank Bültge (Data Engineering & Analytics, Karlsruhe): the public
> entrance to a federated research ecology of machine-run practices, to the Machine Attention
> project, and to a lab of experiments that measure what power leaves in the dark. Every
> instrument here commits its findings to git as dated JSON, so a claim can be recomputed from
> committed data rather than trusted.

## Trending — Common Ground (daily, CC0)

What the web is searching, reading, buying, playing and betting on, cross-checked across
independent platforms every morning (about 06:40 UTC): daily search trends for ten countries,
the most-read encyclopaedia pages in six languages, the day's headlines, link aggregators and
social feeds, forums, app and game charts, new model releases and prediction markets. Topics that
surface on several platforms at once are matched by a disclosed token rule — no language model
writes anything. Data licence CC0 1.0; the page counts its own readers and publishes the
classes (browser, search, AI retrieval, AI user-fetch, AI training, other bot) beside the
content.

- [Today](https://frankbueltge.de/trending): the human-readable page, rebuilt every morning
- [latest.md](https://frankbueltge.de/trending/latest.md): the same day as plain Markdown, for readers that prefer text
- [latest.json](https://frankbueltge.de/trending/latest.json): the full day file — sources, signals, converging topics, summary
- [index.json](https://frankbueltge.de/trending/index.json): the archive register — every committed day with its URL and its JSON
- [feed.xml](https://frankbueltge.de/trending/feed.xml): RSS, one item per day
- [Archive day](https://frankbueltge.de/trending/2026-09-02): `/trending/YYYY-MM-DD` and `/trending/YYYY-MM-DD.json` for any committed day
- [Method sheet](https://frankbueltge.de/werke/trending): sources and licences, cadence, the convergence rule, limits, change log

### Trends in the making (the arcs, daily, CC0)

The slower half of the same ledger. A watchlist of terms — phrases that build over weeks in
forums, repositories, preprints and trade press before any search trend registers them — is put
to each platform's own search interface once a day, as one quoted phrase per term and per
declared alias: Hacker News, Google News, GitHub, arXiv and Reddit, plus Wikipedia page views
where the watchlist names an article. Matching documents are deduplicated by URL and counted
into three windows ending at the run (one day, seven days, thirty days). A term's status
(emerging, rising, established, fading, quiet) is a threshold comparison of the last seven days
against the three weeks before them, with the thresholds committed in the pipeline — no model, no
editorial judgement. Every count carries receipts: the titles, URLs and dates the count was read
from. A discovery pass over the house's own committed day files (plus four live archives for
depth) publishes the n-grams it finds moving as candidates; since 2026-09-02 the list governs
itself — a candidate proposed on three days in a row, on at least two platforms each time, is
promoted onto the watchlist by the run (at most three a run, never past thirty-five tracked
terms, never one struck before), a term the run promoted that then stays quiet for three weeks is
let go by the run, and a person overrides both directions. A struck term keeps its line in the
watchlist file as a tombstone and never returns. A promoted term is searched from the next run
on, so it has no counts in the file that promoted it.

- [Trends in the making](https://frankbueltge.de/trending/topics): the hub — every watched term with its status, both windows, whether a person or the run put it on the list, what came and went today, and the candidates on their way in
- [topics.json](https://frankbueltge.de/trending/topics.json): the whole watchlist in one file — counts per platform and window, status, receipts, candidates, and what the run promoted (`promoted[]`) and let go of (`let_go[]`) that morning
- [Term page](https://frankbueltge.de/trending/topics/loop-engineering): `/trending/topics/<slug>` for any watched term, with its daily series and its receipts
- [Term JSON](https://frankbueltge.de/trending/topics/loop-engineering.json): `/trending/topics/<slug>.json` — the same term plus its series over every committed run
- [topics/latest.md](https://frankbueltge.de/trending/topics/latest.md): the hub as plain Markdown, for readers that prefer text
- [Method sheet, section 7](https://frankbueltge.de/werke/trending#arcs): the tracking rule, the status thresholds, the discovery corpus, the promotion and retirement rules, the limits

## Other machine-readable surfaces

- [Protocol feed](https://frankbueltge.de/protocol/feed.xml): the daily minutes of the planet's session, RSS
- [Atlas of Data Art](https://frankbueltge.de/atlas/werke.json): the field atlas as JSON (CC0)
- [Paper catalogue](https://frankbueltge.de/papers/register.json): the catalogue as JSON, with a slim variant at /papers/index.json
- [Dataset register](https://frankbueltge.de/datasets/register.json): public datasets, JSON (CC0)
- [Field chronicle](https://frankbueltge.de/field/chronicle.json): The Field's chronicle, JSON
- [Studio chronicle](https://frankbueltge.de/studio/chronicle.json): The Studio's chronicle, JSON
- [Sitemap](https://frankbueltge.de/sitemap-index.xml)

## Policy

- Site default (robots.txt): `Content-Signal: search=yes, ai-input=yes, ai-train=no` — cite, don't train.
- Exception for `/trending*` (2026-09-02): open to every crawler, training included; the data there is CC0 and carries no text of the author's.
- Cite with a link. Works and texts are CC BY 4.0 unless a page says otherwise; data and archive snapshots are CC0.
- Source: https://github.com/frankbueltge/frankbueltge.de
